raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This adds opt-in group-wide LoRA admission and residency for MRV2's internal MoE DP path. It follows the draft proposal in #65209.

Stacked on #61714 and #63077. The new work is [this incremental diff](https://github.com/MagellaX/vllm/compare/faf4a54103bee17f479786226c551404427e93ef...fad06f7a16afa54981c28f80f610db7e17704fe1); those prerequisites are included in the main-based diff. The latest [rollback delta](https://github.com/MagellaX/vllm/compare/867a0b4156151f41ae980b6db0b3911f44c91f56...fad06f7a16afa54981c28f80f610db7e17704fe1) is separate for review.

## Claims

- Bound the participating engines' adapter union by `max_loras`, including pins and running requests. Other adapters wait; free slots can be reused while unrelated requests continue.
- Register group-wide IDs so separate frontend counters cannot alias different adapters.
- Load through the existing managers, retire GPU readers before replacement, and publish readiness only after every worker acknowledges matching source fingerprints.
- Keep coordination out of the per-layer path and preserve existing adapter-buffer addresses. The feature is off by default.
- Roll back rejected updates from retained CPU objects, restoring cache order and pins before admission resumes. Lost workers or failed restoration still fail closed.

This does not duplicate the idle-preservation, residency-reporting, or slot-update work: it coordinates admission and eviction across engines rather than only managing each worker's local state.

## Validation

Real OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct with four distinguishable expert-LoRA variants, a two-slot budget, and mixed decode lengths of 64/8/16/32. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` were enabled.

The initial commit `867a0b41` passed:

| Setup | Eager | FULL graph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2× H100 80GB, DP2×TP1 | Passed | Passed; 79 replays per worker |
| 4× H100 80GB, DP2×TP2 | Passed | Passed; 79 replays per worker |

Permuted slots, a cold receiver, divergent residency and four concurrent adapters matched the healthy reference's seven prompt log-probs, generated text and finish reasons exactly within each setup. The earlier eager baseline reproduced `Dispatched MoE LoRA adapter is not resident on this worker` for the cold/divergent cases. The four-adapter demand actually exceeded the two-slot budget.

I also reran the reviewed commit against a manually healthy feature-off server on the same physical GPUs, sequentially within each allocation. Both the 2-GPU and 4-GPU comparisons matched exactly, including FULL graph mode. This is within-topology agreement, not a claim that TP1 and TP2 are bitwise equivalent.

- 15 CPU tests passed on the rollback revision, including real stateless-Gloo exchange, admission progress, partial-readiness rejection, mutation ordering, frontend ID collisions and rejected-update handling.
- All changed-file pre-commit checks passed on Linux, including mypy and CI test tethering. The two GPU tests are selected by the existing LoRA distributed step.
- The CI fixture builder matched all 6,304 tensors in each cached validation variant bit-for-bit. No H200 results are claimed here.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/engine/test_lora_admission.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py -k group_lora_admission
```

Graph validation additionally called `run_group_admission_server(..., graph=True)` from that test module and required observed FULL graph replay calls on every worker, not just successful capture. Pinned model/adapter revisions were `b89a7c4bc24fb9e55ce2543c9458ce0ca5c4650e` / `173c24a401b96703ba97256d5a2f4d4c4c1915a6`.

Rollback revision `fad06f7a` passed on both topologies:

- Missing, corrupt and mismatched worker-local weights, delayed acknowledgement, restored cache order/pins, unchanged buffer addresses and exact outputs.
- FULL graph recovery, including restoration after the old source disappears and fail-closed behavior after worker loss; 79 replay calls per worker.
- Eager recovery on both topologies. The initial 2-GPU eager pass predates the source-disappearance test; the 4-GPU eager run includes it.
- Public async pin/exhaustion checks passed on both topologies. The 4-GPU campaign reached its 15-minute limit after correctness and benchmarks completed; the pin check passed in a separate short allocation with fresh topology checks and the same source. No completed cases were rerun or waived.

The old production commit `867a0b41`, with the new recovery helper, failed on missing weights: `Group LoRA preparation failed; admission blocked`, dead engines and a timed-out load request. The updated code returns the load error and keeps serving the previous adapters. Saved FULL graph outputs also match the earlier feature-off oracle exactly within each topology/mode; no cross-mode equivalence is claimed.

### Performance measurements

Feature off versus native admission on the same physical GPUs, one server under load at a time. Three windows each, interleaved off/on/on/off/off/on; 256 requests/window, concurrency 32, fixed 128-token inputs/outputs, alternating adapters. All 3,072 measured requests completed with zero failures.

| Topology | Off output tokens/s/GPU, median [range] | Native output tokens/s/GPU, median [range] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DP2×TP1 | 1,307 [1,224–1,421] | 1,459 [1,179–1,474] |
| DP2×TP2 | 737 [618–809] | 749 [729–762] |

The ranges overlap; these short synthetic runs do not establish a reliable speedup or a production tail-latency guarantee. No timings were discarded.

<details>
<summary>Latency, memory and benchmark reproduction</summary>

TTFT in ms, median [range] of three per-window statistics:

| Topology / mode | Mean TTFT | Window P99 TTFT | Maximum allocated / reserved GiB per worker |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DP2×TP1 / off | 201.9 [152.3–235.3] | 361.5 [284.4–847.0] | 7.237 / 7.271 |
| DP2×TP1 / native | 166.5 [157.2–186.1] | 376.9 [331.7–420.4] | 7.237 / 7.271 |
| DP2×TP2 / off | 201.7 [199.4–373.5] | 408.8 [337.2–2,433.6] | 3.770 / 3.799 |
| DP2×TP2 / native | 201.3 [190.3–204.7] | 345.2 [342.3–360.2] | 3.770 / 3.801 |

CPU-cache-cold, filesystem-warm registration, three samples each: DP2×TP1 0.828 s [0.802–0.851], then first-request TTFT 25.8 ms [25.5–26.2]; DP2×TP2 0.859 s [0.837–0.910], then TTFT 26.5 ms [23.5–27.8]. These are not uncached downloads or population percentiles.

Both servers stayed resident at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.4`; `max_model_len=512`, `max_num_batched_tokens=512`, `max_num_seqs=32`, `max_loras=2`, `max_cpu_loras=4`, rank 8, prefix caching off. Each received 32 adapter warmup requests before the repeated benchmark. Allocator peaks were reset/read at synchronized boundaries outside timing; device-wide memory snapshots were retained separately and include both resident servers.

```bash
.venv/bin/vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url "$SERVER" --model "$MODEL" \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 128 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.0 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32 \
  --request-rate inf --seed 1 --temperature 0 --ignore-eos \
  --lora-modules adapter-1 adapter-2 --lora-assignment round-robin \
  --num-warmups 16 --save-result --save-detailed --disable-tqdm
```

Manual checks additionally call `run_group_admission_server(MODEL, PATHS, tp, graph=True, failstop=True)` and `asyncio.run(check_group_lora_pins(MODEL, PATHS, tp))` from the same test module (`tp=1/2`). Frozen dependency image `im-sTHRvFs5Vp6w7nfgGd09vp`, Python 3.12.1, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA image 13.0.2; source overlays and raw results carry exact file SHA-256 manifests. The image's package version string reflects its base, not the source overlay.

[2-GPU campaign](https://modal.com/apps/eb01362/main/ap-PWGDCm2lRlKfJ77AElIpmY), [4-GPU campaign](https://modal.com/apps/eb01362/main/ap-P3qGmuwe1CbJjTQck6k0yU), [4-GPU pin continuation](https://modal.com/apps/eb01362/main/ap-rrrBhGXvejiWsH1SwRCsoZ). Raw benchmark JSON, commands and failure logs are retained; these account links may require access.

</details>

## Details

Enable `--enable-group-lora-admission` with `--enable-lora` and `--all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter`. The controller lives separately from the scheduler; the scheduler only checks the admitted IDs.

This stays a draft. Each update retains the previous CPU models until all workers commit, so rollback does not depend on rereading a failed checkpoint. This can temporarily exceed the CPU cache budget; GPU buffer addresses remain stable. Rollback does not restart dead workers or recover invalid CUDA contexts. PP, external/hybrid DP, elastic EP, fault tolerance, streaming inputs, structured outputs and in-place adapter updates remain refused. Multi-node and multi-frontend end-to-end coverage are still outstanding. These are correctness results, not model-quality claims.

Docs are findable locally and on GitHub. The rendered preview is unavailable: [RTD build](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35610032/) stops at the upstream contributor/label pre-run gate, before rendering; local changed-file checks passed.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. Codex helped with implementation and validation; I reviewed the original and rollback diffs and understand the changes.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Isolates the experimental controller and reuses the existing loaders and DP coordination.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Real serving validation, targeted CPU coverage and CI selection are included; remaining coverage is listed above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changed-file checks pass and the new flag and restrictions are documented.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes the stack, reproducer, results and limitations.

</details>

+from vllm.logger import init_logger

+def gather_metadata(group: ProcessGroup, value: Any) -> list[Any]:
+    """Gather CPU metadata without requiring a registered default process group."""
+    encoded = msgspec.msgpack.encode(value)
+    size = torch.tensor([len(encoded)], dtype=torch.int64, device="cpu")
+    sizes = [torch.empty_like(size) for _ in range(group.size())]
+    group.allgather([sizes], [size]).wait()
+    buffer = torch.zeros(
+        max(int(item.item()) for item in sizes), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cpu"
+    )
+    buffer[: len(encoded)] = torch.frombuffer(bytearray(encoded), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    buffers = [torch.empty_like(buffer) for _ in sizes]
+    group.allgather([buffers], [buffer]).wait()
+    return [
+        msgspec.msgpack.decode(item[: int(length.item())].numpy().tobytes())
+        for item, length in zip(buffers, sizes)
+    ]

+    @staticmethod

+    def validate(self, action: tuple[str, Any], reports: list[dict]) -> dict[int, str]:
+        if not reports or any(report["error"] for report in reports):

+                    )

+            expected = {
+                msgspec.msgpack.decode(argument, type=LoRARequest).lora_int_id
+                if method == "add_lora"
+                else argument
+            }
+            if any(set(report["fingerprints"]) != expected for report in reports):
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    "Not every worker acknowledged the registered adapter"
+                )
+        if method == "prepare":
+            desired = frozenset(
+                msgspec.msgpack.decode(item, type=LoRARequest).lora_int_id
+                for item in argument
+            )
+            if any(set(report["fingerprints"]) != desired for report in reports):
+                raise RuntimeError(

+                )

+    def reject(self, action: tuple[str, Any], error: str) -> set[int]:
+        self.admitted = self.ready
+        message = f"Group LoRA update failed; previous epoch restored: {error}"
+        if action[0] == "prepare":

+        self.target = None
+        future.set_exception(ValueError(message))

+        self.fingerprints.update(identities)
